title: (No AI) OpenAI is stepping back from NDAs for data center projects
author: Jay Peters
content:
![Graphic image of a data center.](https://platform.theverge.com/wp-content/uploads/sites/2/2026/06/STKS528_DATA_CENTERS2_B.jpg?quality=90&strip=all&crop=0,0,100,100)

Following this week's midterms where voters resoundingly voiced their [opposition to data center expansion](https://www.theverge.com/policy/1026365/data-centers-midterms-results), OpenAI today announced [new commitments](https://openai.com/index/setting-new-standard-responsible-ai-infrastructure/) to communities where it is working on data center projects, including that it won't use non-disclosure agreements (NDAs) with public officials.

Many data center projects have come under scrutiny for relying on NDAs to [hide discussions](https://www.npr.org/2026/08/27/nx-s1-5879528/data-center-nda-disclosure-louisiana) between developers and local officials. However, OpenAI says it is now allowing "only narrow protections covering legitimate security information, trade secrets, or proprietary or competitively sensitive information." In October, Amazon announced [it would](https://www.theverge.com/tech/1003929/amazon-ai-data-center-blog-warning) no longer u …

[Read the full story at The Verge.](https://www.theverge.com/ai-artificial-intelligence/1028454/openai-data-center-nda)

title: (No AI) Airbnb is working on an AI travel agent
author: Jay Peters
content:
![An image showing the Airbnb logo](https://platform.theverge.com/wp-content/uploads/sites/2/2025/04/acastro_STK090_06.jpg?quality=90&strip=all&crop=0,0,100,100)

Airbnb plans to roll out an AI agent in the first half of 2027 that will help users plan and book travel, the company said in its Q3 2026 earnings shareholder letter [released today](https://s26.q4cdn.com/656283129/files/content_files/Airbnb-Q3-2026-Shareholder-Letter.pdf).

"Today's AI agents are good at simple, routine tasks, like making a restaurant reservation or scheduling an appointment," Airbnb said. "But planning a trip on Airbnb is different." The company argued that its experience matching hosts and guests, its current role in being part of reservations already, and a "new interface" built "specifically for travel" gives it an edge.
